key_insight: C-ReD provides the first comprehensive Chinese benchmark for detecting AI-generated text built from real-world prompts, combining diverse LLM outputs, human references, and standardized evaluation to improve detector robustness.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of model diversity and data homogeneity in existing Chinese AI-generated-text corpora, which limits generalization and real-world applicability of detection methods.
method: Collect large-scale, real-world prompts covering multiple domains and writing styles from Chinese platforms.
Generate outputs using a diverse set of LLMs (commercial and open-source) and pair them with human-written counterparts.
Manually curate/label texts and provide rich metadata plus standardized evaluation protocols and baseline detector results.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to benchmark and develop more robust Chinese detectors that generalize across models and real-world prompts, reducing blind spots in deployment and evaluation.
visual_elements: Dataset composition pie chart showing proportion by source (human vs. each LLM) and domain breakdown (news, social, education, etc.).
Pipeline diagram: prompt collection → multi-LLM generation → annotation/curation → benchmark & evaluation.
Heatmap or grouped bar chart comparing baseline detector performance across different LLMs and domains.
Side-by-side example panel showing a prompt, AI-generated vs. human text, and annotation/metadata tags.
paper_title: C-ReD: A Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for AI-Generated Text Detection Derived from Real-World Prompts
paper_authors: Chenxi Qing, Junxi Wu, Zheng Liu, Yixiang Qiu, Hongyao Yu
